# NEX — Neural Execution Language

NEX is a checked programming language and toolchain for humans and LLMs.
This checkout builds the toolchain 1.0.0 release candidate with compiler fallback language 0.28 and task ABIs 7/8.
It includes ordinary source contracts and experimental checked scalar Metal
emission with installed owned-provider preparation tools. Complete matching
portable SDK qualification remains pending. The current README links exact
source/device records; older SDK archives keep their own versioned evidence.
Ordinary projects select 0.28, 0.29 or 0.30. `nex init` selects 0.30. Typed cells
and state have reference/native/TypeScript execution, guarded graph migration,
static components, request-owned HTTP contexts and versioned task capture/replay.
The source libraries include persistent sequences, queues, stacks, heaps, hash
maps and sets. Use `std/insertion_ordered_map.nex` when iteration must follow
key insertion order. [Map operations and costs](docs/insertion-ordered-map.md)
Persistent 0.30 browser state uses serialized source tasks and copied wire views.
Checked native tasks can share an application-owned heap across static libraries
and fixed shared libraries using ABI8. Keep each library loaded until its tasks
and returned values retire. Query `managed_references.source030_development.native_providers`
for the installed compiler's capabilities. Parallel reference transfer, runtime
library unloading and full Java/Python semantics remain pending.
[Native provider lifetime](docs/reference-task-providers.md)
Executables run without an LLM. Precise semantics and small retrieved contexts are design goals;
the first local Qwen3.8 27B comparison found no NEX token savings.

Start with the affected source, test and coding contract. Query `nex describe --field PATH --json` for a needed feature, or the index for unknown fields.
Read a live function with `nex context ENTRY --kind brief --symbol NAME --json`.
For native hosts, query the bounded
[`native_entry_abi`](docs/native-entry-abi.md) in library build JSON. Retrieve the
actual physical signature and hidden error output; a symbol name alone is not
a host prototype. Discover availability in the selected compiler first.
The selected compiler and actual tests govern support. PLAN and historical
experiments are not implemented capability lists. Current Windows CUDA and CIX
GPU/NPU checks retain their exact source and
ordinary-installation scope. Scalar Metal emission is experimental; broader
GPU/NPU compilation, Apple NPU and complete matching platform/SDK qualification
remain open. Query `gpu_codegen` and `gpu_codegen.owned_provider` before use.
